researched_by: the council's own parking, leisure and car park order pages; the Business Gateway grant page for the region's aires scheme; local press on the aires programme; a documented council email exchange about the picnic-area signs; and Forestry and Land Scotland's own pages for the Galloway Forest holding, which is a separate register entry
policy_summary:
Dumfries and Galloway is the first authority in the dataset that tried to solve motorhome provision by paying other people to provide it, and then stopped. Its own car parks contain no designated bays, no aire, no waste point programme and no overnight permit. What it did instead, from about 2021, was run an Aires (Motorhome Stopover) Grant through Business Gateway: up to 50 per cent of costs to a maximum of GBP3,000 per site, for signage, markings, black and grey water disposal and lighting, aimed at private landowners and community bodies. The strategy put to the Economy and Resources Committee targeted fifteen new aires of roughly four bays each, about 22,000 bay-nights a year at an assumed 41 per cent occupancy, around GBP90,000 of aire revenue and over GBP500,000 of wider local spend. The pilot was Kirkcudbright Swimming Pool, which took GBP1,000, built three spaces with electric and waste disposal, and took 121 overnight stays and GBP1,334 in its first season. Applicants were steered to Certified Location or MotorhomeFun exemption status so that five vans or fewer needed no planning permission. The grant page is now marked CLOSED and retained for reference only.

On its own estate the council went the other way, and it did so with signs. From 2022-23 'no camping or overnight parking' signage went up in car parks and picnic areas, most visibly across Wigtownshire, put there at the request of community councils after complaints about camping and waste. Asked directly about New England Bay, the council's own reply was that 'presently these signs are not enforceable in law', that the restriction covers 'the whole area as you enter into New England bay', and - the significant part - that 'the proposals are for all the car parks in Dumfries & Galloway not just New England bay'. So the intent is region-wide and the legal backing is nil.

Nothing found since closes that gap. The Dumfries and Galloway Council (Various Vehicle Parking Places) (Use and Waiting Restrictions) Parking Places Order 2023 consolidated a 1985 order and was consulted on to 30 June 2023, but its published six-point statement of reasons is about traffic management, enforcement efficiency, town centre viability, contravention codes, EV charging bays and consolidation. Overnight parking, sleeping, motorhomes, camping and caravans appear nowhere in it. The Regional Parking Strategy consulted on September to November 2023 lists its themes as supply and demand, facilities, enforcement, signage, the Transport (Scotland) Act 2019 and charges - again, no motorhome strand. The live parking pages mention motorhomes not once.

What the council does own and run is two full touring caravan parks, and they are the only reliable council-provided overnight stops in the region: Lochside at Castle Douglas on Carlingwark Loch, 100 caravan and motorhome pitches plus 50 tent pitches, open March to January; and Kirk Loch at Lochmaben, 30 pitches, April to the last Sunday in October. These are campsites at campsite prices - GBP29.50 to GBP38 a night in 2026 - not aires, and they sit under leisure and tourism, nowhere near the parking pages.

For a van user the practical position is: two proper council sites at full price, a scatter of small private aires the council part-funded and does not list, an FLS scheme in the forest that is not the council's, and everywhere else a sign the council has admitted it cannot enforce.
notes:
THE DARK SKY CHECK - THE EXMOOR SPLIT DOES NOT HOLD HERE, AND THE REASON IS OWNERSHIP. The hypothesis was that a Dark Sky Park would encourage night visiting while banning overnight vehicle stays, as Exmoor does. In Galloway the opposite is true, because the dark sky sits on someone else's land. Galloway Forest Park has been an International Dark Sky Park since 2009 and holds Gold Tier status; the land is Forestry and Land Scotland, a separate register entry, and its records must not be filed here. FLS both encourages night visiting - its dark skies page gives stargazing advice and names Clatteringshaws Loch, Stroan Loch and Glentrool as viewing spots - AND sells overnight vehicle stays at those same places under Stay the Night, at GBP10 a night (GBP13 where there is chemical disposal), one night only, 6pm to 10am, no return within 48 hours, self-contained motorhomes and campervans only. Stroan Loch is simultaneously a recommended stargazing spot and a three-space Stay the Night car park. Glentrool has ten spaces, Kirroughtree thirty, Raiders' Road three sub-sites of three, Red Deer Range and Wild Goat Park four each, plus Black Loch three, Dalbeattie four and Forest of Ae eight. So in Galloway the dark-sky landowner has monetised sleeping rather than prohibited it, and the parking-versus-sleeping split found at Exmoor is absent. Record none of it under this authority; it belongs to Forestry and Land Scotland.

THE COUNCIL'S OWN ADMISSION IS THE MOST USEFUL LINE IN THE FILE. 'Presently these signs are not enforceable in law' is Exmoor's parenthesis said out loud by the body that put the signs up. It puts Dumfries and Galloway in the same legal class as Exmoor - prohibition by conditions of entry, enforceable by asking you to leave, not by penalty - but with the council on record rather than a researcher inferring it. The signs also did not originate with the council: they came from community council requests. That matters for direction of travel, because pressure from below with no instrument behind it is exactly the configuration that later produces a real order.

THE STRUCTURAL FINDING: THIS IS PROVISION BY PROXY AND IT HAS BEEN WOUND UP. Compare South Ayrshire, which built the bays itself, kept the revenue, made the trial permanent and expanded twice; and Pembrokeshire, where each revision made the scheme smaller. Dumfries and Galloway did neither. It bought fifteen small aires it does not own, cannot list, cannot guarantee and cannot re-price, then closed the grant. The result is invisible supply: the sites exist on park4night and SearchForSites, not on any council page, so the authority appears to provide nothing while having quietly seeded a network. This is a distinct third pattern and worth its own line in the hostility index - an authority can score zero on provision and still have caused provision to exist.

Also: a GBP3,000 cap steering applicants to a five-van planning exemption is a deliberate choice for many tiny sites rather than a few real ones. That is the opposite of the capital-investment logic in section 3 of the method doc, and it is why none of these sites persist as recorded infrastructure.

SCOTTISH ACCESS RIGHTS DO NOT HELP. Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2003 access rights cover access on foot and do not extend to motorhomes or any other vehicle. Nothing in this file may be read as a right to sleep in a vehicle anywhere in the region.

NATIONAL PARK CONTEXT: the Galloway National Park proposal was dropped by the Scottish Government in May 2025 after NatureScot's consultation, with the council itself having stayed neutral. Had it gone ahead there would now be a fifteenth UK national park authority owning car parks here, on the Cairngorms and Loch Lomond model. There is not, so this council and FLS remain the two bodies that matter.

PRIVATE SUPPLY, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-RESEARCHES IT: New England Bay has a Camping and Caravanning Club site alongside the council picnic area, open roughly six months a year. Kirkcudbright Swimming Pool's three-space aire is community-run and grant-aided, not council-run. The wider region's commercial parks (Pitchup and campsites.co.uk both list 35-plus) are private. None of these are council provision and none are recorded here.

ENFORCEMENT REALITY: no evidence of ANPR, patrol, fixed penalties or PCNs for overnight stays anywhere on the council estate. The Car Park Order 2023 brought decriminalised-style contravention codes to off-street parking, but for tariff and bay-misuse offences, not for sleeping. The realistic worst case remains a knock on the window.
open_questions: Does the full text of the Parking Places Order 2023 - the schedules, not the statement of reasons - contain any overnight, sleeping or vehicle-type prohibition? The council publishes only the introduction and reasons online; the order itself has to be requested from the Head of Roads and Infrastructure at Militia House. This is the single unresolved legal question in the file.

Did the region-wide 'no overnight parking in all car parks' proposal the council described in correspondence ever become anything? No order, decision, committee report or consultation implementing it was found, three years on.

How many aires did the grant actually create, and where are they? The strategy targeted fifteen; only the Kirkcudbright pilot is documented by name. No council list of funded sites was found and there may never have been one.
Why was the Aires grant closed - budget, Business Gateway restructuring, or a decision that it had done its job? The page gives no reason.

Do the council's harbours (Kirkcudbright, Portpatrick, Isle of Whithorn, Garlieston, Drummore) permit or sell overnight vehicle stays? The harbours pages returned 403 on every attempt and this remains unchecked. Portpatrick in particular is a likely candidate.
Exact 2026 maximum stay at Lochside and Kirk Loch. The council publishes nightly, 7-night and 14-night tariffs but states no maximum.
Precise coordinates for the New England Bay picnic area and car park, and whether the signs are still up in 2026.

sites.name: Lochside Caravan Park, Castle Douglas
sites.operator: Dumfries and Galloway Council (in-house; direct council phone line and council mailbox)
facilities: 100 caravan and motorhome pitches, hardstanding or grass
electric hook-up on service pitches only
sites.search_hint: Lochside Caravan Park, Carlingwark Loch, Lochside Park, Castle Douglas
sites.notes:
THE STEP-2 CATEGORY: a council-owned, council-operated touring caravan park that no parking page links to and that links to no parking page. It lives under leisure, sport and culture - things to do - not under roads, transport and parking. Contact is lochside@dumfriesandgalloway.gov.uk and 01556 504682, both council-run, so operation is in-house and not leased out.

SEASON: open March to January, closed February for maintenance. That eleven-month season is unusually long for a Scottish council site and makes this the region's only realistic year-round council stop.

PRICE (2026 council tariff): caravan and motorhome pitches GBP29.50 to GBP33 a night standard, GBP35.50 to GBP38 on service pitches with hook-up, water and TV point. Weekly GBP177-GBP217.50 standard and GBP213-GBP253 service; fortnightly GBP354-GBP397 and GBP426-GBP463. Tents GBP19 to GBP35.50 by party size and services. The GBP29.50 base rate is what is recorded here. Note the ranges: the council publishes a band rather than one figure, which usually means seasonal or pitch-type variation it does not explain.

This is a campsite, not an aire. There is no short-stopover product, no motorhome service point sold separately, and no evidence non-residents can buy waste disposal alone. Assume you must book a pitch.

Size is the point: 150 pitches makes this by some distance the largest single piece of council overnight capacity found in Scotland so far, and it is entirely absent from any motorhome-facing council page.
sites.geocode_precision: unit postcode centroid for DG7 1EZ, the address the council itself publishes for the caravan park (Carlingwark Loch, Lochside Park); the site occupies the north-east shore of Carlingwark Loch immediately south of Castle Douglas town centre
sites.geocode_corroboration: postcodes.io returns 54.936601 / -3.930001 for DG7 1EZ and places it in admin district Dumfries and Galloway, which agrees with the council's published address for the park. Not corroborated at car-park level by a second independent pin, so the band is approximate rather than precise.

sites.name: Kirk Loch Caravan Park, Lochmaben
facilities: electric hook-up, water tap and TV point on service pitches only
male and female toilet and shower blocks
free use of Kirk Loch for boating or fishing (no petrol engines)
sites.search_hint: Kirk Loch Caravan Park, Castlehill Gate, Lochmaben
sites.notes:
The second of the council's two in-house caravan parks, and the smaller one: 30 pitches taking caravans, motorhomes and tents, at Castlehill Gate beside Kirk Loch. Contact 07824 528467 and a council mailbox.

SEASON: bookings run 1 April to the last Sunday in October - a conventional seven-month Scottish season, in contrast to Lochside's eleven months. If you are travelling the region between November and March, Lochside is the only council site open.

PRICE: identical published tariff to Lochside - GBP29.50 to GBP33 standard and GBP35.50 to GBP38 with services, per night, with the same weekly and fortnightly bands. One tariff covering both sites confirms these are run as a single council operation rather than two inherited district sites priced separately.

Inland, not coastal: this is in Annandale, well east of the Solway tourist coast and about 45km from Castle Douglas. It is a useful overnight on the A709/A74(M) corridor rather than a destination for the Solway or the Machars.

sites.name: Aires (Motorhome Stopover) Grant - region-wide funding scheme
sites.operator: Dumfries and Galloway Council via Business Gateway Dumfries and Galloway; the aires themselves are run by private landowners and community bodies, not by the council
sites.search_hint: Aires Motorhome Stopover Grant Business Gateway Dumfries and Galloway
sites.notes:
RECORDED AT NETWORK LEVEL, NOT AS A PLACE. This is the defining feature of the Dumfries and Galloway regime and it has no geometry, because the council funded aires rather than building them.

STATUS: the Business Gateway page is marked CLOSED and retained for reference only. Recorded as 'revoked' to mean no longer available, not to imply an order was struck down.

TERMS while it ran: up to 50 per cent of project costs, maximum GBP3,000 per site. Eligible costs were signage, site markings, site improvements, web design, black and grey water disposal, and lighting. Applicants had to be a legal entity registered with HMRC or Companies House no more than twelve months before applying, under Enterprise Seed Fund terms. Minimum three motorhome capacity, at least four metres between units, safe road access, a What3Words location for emergency services, and promotion through platforms such as park4night. Recommended charge GBP5 to GBP10 a night - the GBP7.50 midpoint is what is recorded in price_per_night, and it is an indicative recommendation to grantees, NOT a price the council charges anywhere.

PLANNING ROUTE: sites that were not already campsites or car parks were steered to Certified Location status, allowing up to five motorhomes without planning permission; more than five needed permission. MotorhomeFun issued exemption certificates under the Caravan Sites and Control of Development Act 1960 and the council set up a streamlined process for them. Scotland's relaxed three-van rule, extended to October 2022, was the other route.

SCALE INTENDED: the Economy and Resources Committee paper targeted fifteen new aires at about four bays each - roughly 22,000 bay-nights a year, 41 per cent assumed occupancy, about GBP90,000 of aire revenue and over GBP500,000 of additional local spend. Committee chair Cllr Rob Davidson called it 'an excellent proposal, and one that proved very popular in our initial trial last year'.

THE PILOT: Kirkcudbright Swimming Pool took GBP1,000, created three spaces with electric points and waste disposal, opened in September, and reported 121 overnight stays, 31 waste disposals and GBP1,334 in its first period, with GBP5,000-GBP6,000 a year projected. The operators said 'the site runs itself with little need to do anything, the extra income will offset the massive rise in our energy costs'. That site is community-run and is NOT recorded as council provision.

WHY IT MATTERS: an authority with zero council-run bays nonetheless caused an unknown number of small aires to exist, and none of them appear on any council page. Any hostility index built from council-published provision alone will score this region wrongly.

sites.name: All Dumfries and Galloway Council car parks and picnic areas
sites.notes:
THE ESTATE-WIDE RECORD, AND THE COUNCIL HAS SAID IN WRITING THAT IT IS UNENFORCEABLE. 'No camping or overnight parking' signage has gone up in council car parks and picnic areas since about 2022-23. Asked about it, the council replied that 'presently these signs are not enforceable in law', that the signs went up 'from a request from local community councils', that there had been 'numerous complaints about camping in all the picnic areas in Wigtownshire', and that 'the proposals are for all the car parks in Dumfries & Galloway not just New England bay'.

SO THE SCOPE IS REGION-WIDE INTENT AND THE LEGAL BACKING IS NONE. The wording covers both limbs - 'no camping' reaches sleeping, 'no overnight parking' reaches the vehicle whether or not anyone is in it - which is why restricts is 'both' and applies_to is 'all_vehicles' rather than a motorhome-specific definition. Nothing in the signage distinguishes a motor caravan from a car.

NO INSTRUMENT WAS FOUND. The Dumfries and Galloway Council (Various Vehicle Parking Places) (Use and Waiting Restrictions) Parking Places Order 2023, which consolidated the 1985 order and closed to objections on 30 June 2023, publishes a six-point statement of reasons covering traffic management and congestion, enforcement and non-compliance, town centre viability, contravention provisions, EV charging bay enforcement and consolidation. Overnight parking, sleeping, camping, motorhomes and caravans appear in none of the six. The Regional Parking Strategy consulted September to November 2023 lists no motorhome strand either. Status is therefore 'unknown' rather than 'in_force': the signs are up and the rule is asserted, but nothing was found that makes it law, and the council itself says it is not.

PRACTICAL EFFECT: same legal class as Exmoor. Conditions of entry, enforceable by being asked to leave, not by penalty charge or prosecution. No ANPR, no patrols, no FPNs and no PCNs for overnight stays were found anywhere in the region.

VOLATILITY WARNING: this is the configuration - community pressure, signs already up, an order recently consolidated - from which a real prohibition usually emerges. Re-check the Parking Places Order and any variation orders before relying on the unenforceability finding.

sites.name: New England Bay picnic area and car park, Rhins of Galloway
facilities: chemical toilet (elsan) disposal point installed by the council
sites.search_hint: New England Bay picnic area and car park, near Drummore, Rhins of Galloway
sites.notes:
THE CONTRADICTION WORTH KEEPING, AND THE CASE THAT PRODUCED THE COUNCIL'S ADMISSION. New England Bay is a rural car park and picnic area on the east shore of the Rhins, with toilets and room for roughly thirty vans. The council installed a chemical toilet disposal point here - a piece of motorhome infrastructure, paid for by the council, in direct response to waste being dumped - and then put up 'no camping or overnight parking' signs covering, in its own words, 'the whole area as you enter into New England bay'.

So the same authority built the facility that only overnight motorhome users need and then signed against overnight motorhome users, in the same place, within about a year. That is the sharpest single illustration in the dataset of provision and prohibition being decided by different departments answering different complainants.

The council's reply about these signs - 'presently these signs are not enforceable in law' - is the source of the estate-wide finding recorded above.

COORDINATES NOT RECORDED. The picnic area could not be located to car-park precision from any source read, and no postcode for it was established. Per protocol lat/lon are null rather than guessed. It is on the A716 coast road south of Sandhead and north of Drummore. NOTE for whoever pins it: the adjacent Camping and Caravanning Club site of the same name is a DIFFERENT place, private, open about six months a year, and must not be pinned in mistake for the council picnic area.
